policies.title: FRONTIER Act
policies.question: Does the speaker support the named FRONTIER Act (H.R. 9925), including its national requirements for advanced AI developers? General support for frontier AI rules is not enough.

policies.title: AI Kill Switch Act
policies.question: Does the speaker support the AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917)? General shutdown safeguards, car kill switches, SB 1047, and a different Senate bill do not establish a position on this House bill.

policies.title: Stop Stealing Our Chips Act
policies.question: Does the speaker support the named Stop Stealing Our Chips Act and its export-enforcement whistleblower incentives/protections? Do not substitute the CHIPS Act or Chip Security Act.

policies.title: AI export controls
policies.question: Does the speaker support restrictions or enforcement on overseas access to advanced AI chips, manufacturing equipment, models, or compute? Opposition to one rule alongside support for narrower controls is mixed or qualified support, with the distinction in the reason. Chip investment alone is irrelevant.

policies.title: Embedded independent auditors (IVOs)
policies.question: Does the speaker support independent verification organizations (IVOs) embedded in AI labs, with ongoing/on-site internal access? Ordinary third-party audits or pre-release tests alone are NOT embedded oversight. Require explicit embedded, on-site, resident, or continuous internal access. General IVO accreditation without embedded access is not relevant to this narrower question.

policies.title: China race dynamics
policies.question: Does the speaker endorse making competition with China a priority for US AI policy? Oppose means rejecting this race framing, not hostility toward China. Label the explicit tradeoffs separately: speed over safety, safety despite competition, cooperation, race skepticism, restrictive exports, or export access to spread US technology. A China mention alone is neutral or irrelevant.

policies.title: America's AI Action Plan (2025)
policies.question: Does the speaker support the Trump administration's July 2025 AI Action Plan? Do not infer support for the whole plan from support for one component. Clear overall endorsement with conditions is support. Use mixed only when the speaker explicitly supports some parts and opposes others without a clear overall endorsement.

policies.title: National AI Legislative Framework (2026)
policies.question: Does the speaker support the White House's March 2026 national AI legislative framework? Generic calls for a national framework are not a position on this specific proposal.

policies.title: Great American AI Act framework
policies.question: Does the speaker support the named Great American AI Act discussion draft/framework? Do not transfer a FRONTIER Act position to the broader framework unless the speaker adopts it too.

policies.title: White House AI Accord (2026)
policies.question: Does the speaker support the September 2026 White House AI Accord? A statement can support this voluntary accord while also wanting binding law. Do not transfer support to an unrelated bill.
